solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Dance with an energy beyond fabulous, initially

indicators.note: beyond says the pieces before it come after the fabulous letter
initially asks for the opening letter of the word fabulous

parts.note: and means with, joining things together
go means energy or vigour, as in full of go

explanation.surface: A dancer adds extra energy to an already fabulous routine.
explanation.definitionFit: A fandango is a lively Spanish courtship dance in triple time, so it is an example of a dance.

clue.text: Fear rout, at first, in conflict

indicators.note: in says the letter goes inside the conflict word

parts.note: a fight is a conflict or battle

indicators.note: at first asks for the opening letter of the word rout

explanation.surface: Soldiers fear a rout in the early stages of a battle.
explanation.definitionFit: A fright is a sudden feeling of fear or alarm.

clue.text: Bloke about to lick up jelly

indicators.note: in a down clue up says the whole assembly is read from bottom to top
about says the man word goes round the licking word

parts.note: a bloke is a man
to lap is to lick up liquid, as a cat does

explanation.surface: A man about to lick up a bowl of jelly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns MLAPAN round; 'jelly' looks like a dessert, but napalm is a jellied fuel.
explanation.definitionFit: Napalm is jellied petrol used as an incendiary weapon, a fiery jelly.

clue.text: Keen to have creative work around the office

indicators.note: around says the art word wraps the office word

parts.note: art is creative work like painting
a den is a private room or study where one works

explanation.surface: An eager employee wants art on display around the workplace.
explanation.definitionFit: Ardent means passionate and enthusiastic, which is what keen means.

clue.text: Criminal group leading old man the wrong way — that sounds aggressive

parts.note: a gang is a band of criminals
a star is the leading player, so leading can mean star

indicators.note: the wrong way says the old man word is read backwards

parts.note: pa is father, informally the old man

explanation.surface: A gang boss marching their elderly father off the wrong way sounds menacing.
explanation.definitionFit: Gangsta rap is a hip-hop style with violent, confrontational lyrics, music with a hostile sound.

clue.text: Crawler once more swims backwards?

indicators.note: backwards tells us to read the whole of 'once more swims' from the end

parts.note: re- is the prefix meaning again, once more
dips means takes a quick swim

explanation.surface: A question about a swimmer doing laps in backstroke one more time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crawler' suggests a front-crawl swimmer, but it is the eight-legged creature; 'backwards' turns REDIPS round.
explanation.definitionFit: A spider is a creeping creature, and anything that creeps along can be called a crawler.

clue.text: Heptagon-shaped virus, perhaps?

indicators.note: shaped means formed into a new shape, so the letters of heptagon are rearranged

explanation.surface: A question about a virus with seven sides.
explanation.definitionFit: A virus is one example of a pathogen, any agent that causes disease, so 'perhaps' marks it as a type.

clue.text: Brilliant banger

definitions.meaning: a firework or explosive that goes off with a bang

explanation.surface: Praise for an excellent firework or excellent sausage.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain a banger is also a sausage, a sense that pulls the eye away from explosives.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for excellent is one sense, and a high explosive that goes bang is the literal one.

clue.text: Warning related to switch under top of roof

indicators.note: in a down clue under says the rearranged letters sit below the roof letter
top of asks for the first letter of the word roof
to switch means to swap about, so the letters of related are rearranged

explanation.surface: An alarm linked to a switch beneath the roof, like a smoke alarm.
explanation.definitionFit: A red alert is the highest state of emergency readiness, an urgent warning of danger.

clue.text: This crossword writer's locked up having stolen Mudd's heart — that's shameless

parts.note: the setter speaking of himself says I am, shortened to I'm

indicators.note: having stolen says the confined word takes something into its middle

parts.note: pent, as in pent up, means shut in or confined

indicators.note: heart asks for the central letters of the setter's name

explanation.surface: The setter confesses to a cheeky theft from his own name.
explanation.definitionFit: Impudent behaviour is cheeky and shows no respect or shame, so the two are close synonyms.

clue.text: Wasted, like plums and peaches?

definitions.meaning: slang for very drunk or high on drugs
fruit with a hard stone at the centre, or fruit with the stones taken out

explanation.surface: Someone worse for wear is compared with a bowl of stone fruit.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang for intoxicated is a common sense, and fruit having stones, or having them removed, is the literal sense.

clue.text: Sanctity required by army not quite closing off borders

indicators.note: closing off means shutting something in, so the shortened army word encloses the next piece
not quite tells us to drop the last letter of the army word

parts.note: a host is a large army or multitude
lines can be boundaries or borders

explanation.surface: A military report about an army failing to seal the frontiers.
explanation.definitionFit: Holiness is the state of being holy or sacred, which is what sanctity means.

clue.text: Short man's stiff

indicators.note: short says the phrase loses its last letter

parts.note: something that is a man's is for a male, written here as one run

explanation.surface: A remark that a little fellow is rigid or awkward.
explanation.walkthrough: 'man's' is read as 'for male' (belonging to a man), which, cut short, runs together as FORMAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Stiff manners are rigid and ceremonious, which is what formal behaviour is.

clue.text: Hot in Sweden, you suspect, in children's home

indicators.note: suspect means dubious or not genuine, so these letters are rearranged

parts.note: H is the abbreviation for hot, as on taps

explanation.surface: A worry that it's warm in Sweden, inside an orphanage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'children's home' looks like an orphanage, but it is a playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: A Wendy house is a toy playhouse for children, named after Wendy in Peter Pan, so literally a home for children.

clue.text: One temporarily leading talk about to stop, gutted

indicators.note: about says the talk word goes round the next piece

parts.note: patter is glib, rapid talk, like a salesman's

indicators.note: gutted says the middle letter is taken out

parts.note: to cease means to stop

explanation.surface: A speaker's chatter is about to stop and they feel gutted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' takes the middle A out of CEASE, leaving CESE.
explanation.definitionFit: A pacesetter leads a race for a while to set the speed, often dropping back later.

clue.text: Impeccable chefs ultimately unable to cook?

indicators.note: ultimately asks for the final letter of the word chefs

parts.note: potless means having no pot, so no way to cook

explanation.surface: Faultless chefs who in the end can't cook.
explanation.definitionFit: Spotless means without any mark or flaw, so faultless or impeccable.

clue.text: Tower over pit maintained by dynamo

indicators.note: maintained by says the pit word is held inside the dynamo word

parts.note: a dynamo is an energetic person, a doer
a pit is a coal mine

explanation.surface: A pithead tower kept running by a generator.
explanation.definitionFit: To domineer is to dominate others overbearingly, to loom over them in power.

clue.text: Second plane is behind

parts.note: to second a proposal is to back it
a side is a flat face or surface, a plane of a solid

explanation.surface: A second aircraft lags behind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'behind' looks like a preposition, but it is the noun for the buttocks.
explanation.definitionFit: Backside and behind are both informal nouns for the buttocks.

clue.text: In discussion, just look for disinformation

indicators.note: in discussion means as heard in speech, signalling a soundalike

parts.note: proper means just or fitting, and a gander is a look, as in take a gander

explanation.surface: A debater urges people to examine claims for misleading information.
explanation.definitionFit: Propaganda is biased or misleading material spread to promote a cause, a form of disinformation.

clue.text: I don't know a couple of old kings

indicators.note: a couple of means two, so the king's name appears twice

parts.note: Tut is the familiar name of Tutankhamun, an ancient Egyptian king

explanation.surface: A shrug of ignorance about some ancient monarchs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I don't know' reads as ignorance, but here it is the exasperated 'I don't know!' of disapproval.
explanation.definitionFit: The tutting sound expresses disapproval, the same tone as an exasperated exclamation of what the world is coming to.

clue.text: Slum preferred over US city

indicators.note: in a down clue over says the preferred word sits above the city

parts.note: fave is informal for favourite, preferred
LA is Los Angeles

explanation.surface: Choosing a slum over an American city.
explanation.definitionFit: A favela is a Brazilian shanty town, an urban slum district.

clue.text: Party turning on inventive mind

indicators.note: turning says the party word is read in reverse

parts.note: a side is a faction or party in a dispute

explanation.surface: A political party switching on a creative thinker.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas Edison was a prolific American inventor, so he stands for an inventive mind.

clue.text: Difficult finding starters served in toilet roll, and disgusting!

indicators.note: starters served in asks for the opening letters of the words that follow

parts.note: icky is informal for nasty or disgusting

explanation.surface: A tricky dinner where the starters are presented in a loo roll.
explanation.definitionFit: Something tricky is hard to handle or needs skill, which matches difficult.

clue.text: Brownish-yellow on you is grand

indicators.note: on says the colour comes after the other piece

parts.note: thou is the old word for you
sand is a pale brownish-yellow colour

explanation.surface: A compliment that a sandy colour looks splendid on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A grand is slang for a thousand pounds or dollars.

clue.text: Papers alongside fish soaking up last of oily batter

indicators.note: alongside says the papers sit beside the fish piece
soaking up says the fish takes in the next letter

parts.note: an eel is a long snake-like fish

indicators.note: last of asks for the final letter of the word oily

parts.note: ID is identity papers

explanation.surface: A fish-and-chip shop scene: newspaper wrapping, fish, and greasy batter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'batter' looks like fish batter, but it means something that bats, as an eyelid does.
explanation.definitionFit: We bat an eyelid when blinking, so the lid is cryptically a batter.

clue.text: Turn revolutionary into Nazi, as Artemis

indicators.note: into says the rearranged letters go inside the Nazi's name

parts.note: Rudolf Hess was Hitler's deputy in the Nazi party

indicators.note: revolutionary suggests a revolt or upheaval, so the letters of turn are rearranged

explanation.surface: A tale of a revolutionary who turns into a Nazi.
explanation.definitionFit: Artemis is the Greek goddess of the hunt, so she is the classic female hunter.

clue.text: Ice hardened around sphere

indicators.note: around says the hardened word wraps the sphere

parts.note: set means firmed up or hardened, like jelly
an orb is a sphere or globe

explanation.surface: Ice that has frozen solid around a ball.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorbet is a water ice, a frozen dessert of fruit juice and sugar.

clue.text: Manacle requires hinge to come down

parts.note: to hinge on something is to rest on it, both meaning to depend
rain is what comes down from the sky

explanation.surface: A handcuff needs its hinge to be lowered.
explanation.definitionFit: To manacle someone is to shackle them, holding them back, as a verb sense of restrain.
